boundary: A LIMITATION THEOREM AND THE BRANCH THAT ESCAPES IT. The machine's q is Phi_d(1), which is 1 or a PRIME -- never a proper prime power -- so the symplectic branch cannot produce W(3,9), W(3,4), W(3,8), W(3,25) or W(3,27). The cause is that pi = 1-zeta is the TOTALLY RAMIFIED prime. Using an unramified prime of Z[zeta_d] gives residue field F_(l^f); a form survives on a single prime iff -1 lies in <l> mod d (conjugation is the adjoint), and it is then HERMITIAN, not alternating. VERIFIED: E8/3E8 = H(3,9) (280 points, 112 lines, 10 per line, 4 per point) and E8/2E8 = H(3,4) (45, 27, 5, 3). The latter REFINES Pass 8925-8940's Q+(7,2) EXACTLY: its 45 isotropic F_4-points expand to the 135 q-singular F_2-points, symmetric difference 0
